newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil Cofap silent on sale talk report.
newsitem.headline: Brazil Cofap silent on sale talk report.

text.p: Brazilian car parts maker Cofap said it would not comment on a newspaper report saying that it is likely to sell a 40 percent voting stake to Italy's car maker Fiat.
"The company will not make any comment on the issue," a Cofap spokeswoman said.

O Estado de Sao Paulo newspaper today said Cofap's shareholders Nelson and Leo Kasinski are holding talks with Fiat's subsidiary Magneti Marelli to sell a 40 percent voting stake in the firm for $80 million.
No officials at Fiat's Brazil unit were immediately available to comment on the report.

The paper also said Abraham Kasinski, the company's president, would sell his 11 percent stake in the firm to Germany's Mahle, Cofap's partner in the local auto parts maker Metal Leve, as he had decided to leave the company.
Kasinski said he would leave the firm on July 11 when he will be 80 years-old, the Cofap spokeswoman said. But she said she could not confirm whether Kasinski will sell his shares to Mahle.
The purchase of the 40 percent stake would give Fiat the same size stake as private bank Bradesco has in Cofap, the paper said.
While the newspaper said Fiat is likely to buy Nelson and Leo Kasinski's 40 percent stake, there were rumors in the market that the Italian company would acquire Bradesco's holdings as well.

U.S. brokerage Bear Stearns said in a report a Fiat purchase of Cofap would make sense given Fiat's strong ties to the firm. It noted that Cofap won a contract as the supplier of suspension systems for Fiat's Palio world car, which recently began production in Brazil.
Cofap also announced last year it would invest $48 million in a plant in Argentina to make shock absorbers for Fiat SpA cars.
